bearings.paper_claim: SLES is a weighted average of 15 indicators: five stage shares (introduced, AIC, ABC, passed chamber, law) at three significance weights (1, 5, 10), normalized by N/5 so each chamber-term averages 1 (Eq. 1). Window 1987-2018, 97 chambers, 80,344 legislator-term scores. Hand audit: 46,693 of 49,037 sampled bills (95.2%) correctly coded, over 99% after revision. North Carolina 2005-2012: SLES explains about half the variation in NCCPPR rankings and beats hit-rate metrics.
bearings.paper_location: Eq. 1 at text lines 363-380 (pp. 23-24); validity lines 506-561 (p. 24)
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/legislative_effectiveness.py: STAGES at line 17; role weights sponsor 3, original 2, cosponsor 1 at lines 18-19; impact weights limited to 1, 5, 10 at line 232; letters forced to weight 5 at line 228; congress_decay 0.8 at lines 29 and 482; normalization N/5 per chamber and Congress at line 500; cosponsor timing multiplier 2 to the power of minus delay over 180 at line 132; status shadow_candidate at line 31. effectiveness_integration.py line 111 holds the 0.7 advocacy and 0.3 results composite. The CU-mention significance source was not found in this file; the weight arrives from an upstream impact record (line 225).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The stage, weight and normalization structure transfers to the federal shadow as a structural adaptation. The paper's validation covers sponsor-based state SLES with newspaper-coded significance; it does not validate cosponsor role credit, the 180-day timing decay, letters at weight 5, or the 70/30 composite. Those stay UNVERIFIED until checked against CEL LES for the same members and Congresses.
bearings.verifier_note: Stage, weight, normalization and decay constants reproduce. Summary says the shadow departs from SLES in two ways, but the bearing lists more (cosponsor credit with timing decay, letters at weight 5, 70/30 composite, upstream significance). The CU-mention significance source was not located in the file. Rewrite departures as the list that code shows.

bearings.paper_claim: In North Carolina 2005-2012 SLES outperforms hit-rate metrics against subjective rankings. Scores are relative to each chamber-term and should not be compared directly across chambers or eras. Majority status adds 0.370 in the pooled full-sample estimate (strata: 0.362 lower chamber, 0.387 upper), 58 percent above the minority mean of 0.636.
bearings.paper_location: Validity p. 24, lines 535-561; comparability pp. 23-24, lines 380-400; Table 1 lines 896-926; 58 percent statement lines 718-720
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/live_legislative_pillar.py lines 74-80: per category, decay-weighted signed share of advanced bills divided by total decay weight, scaled by category maximum, then percentile-ranked across members. fec/engine/compute_pillars.py line 179 uses legislative_percentiles in legacy mode; line 181 divides influence by the cross-member maximum. No majority or minority term appears in these lines, and House and Senate share one roster and one percentile.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The NC criterion covers one state chamber pair over eight years; transfer to Congress is an assumption. The 0.370 figure is an unstratified pooled estimate and must carry strata or an UNSTRATIFIED label, which the rel does.
bearings.verifier_note: All numbers reproduce (Table 1 lines 921-923; lines 718-720). Comparability caution and NC hit-rate claim are in the paper. Code lines checked. The 'largest driver' wording in the gaps section is wrong; see summary_issues.

bearings.paper_claim: Committee chairs score 0.507 above rank-and-file in the pooled full-sample estimate (strata: 0.609 lower chamber, 0.307 upper). The chair gap widens with log chamber size (0.205, p<0.05) and narrows where chambers vote on committee appointments (-0.180, p<0.01). Majority status adds 0.370 (strata 0.362 and 0.387).
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/committee_scores.py lines 125-129 set multipliers Chair 3.0 full and 7.5 sub, Ranking 2.0 and 4.5, Vice 1.0 and 2.0, identical for both chambers. Influence is committee raw divided by the maximum across members (compute_pillars.py line 181), so House and Senate are pooled. No majority-status term.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's estimates are associational with endogeneity unaddressed (p. 34) and do not estimate multipliers. The chamber-size transfer to a 435-seat House and 100-seat Senate is the analyst's extrapolation, not the paper's claim. The Ranking-to-Chair ratio of two-thirds holds only for full weights; for sub weights it is 4.5 over 7.5, or 0.60.
bearings.verifier_note: Chair, majority and strata values reproduce exactly. The two-thirds ratio is right only for full weight; restate sub weight as 0.60. Chamber-size transfer to Congress is an inference and should be labeled as one.

bearings.paper_claim: Stage-based effectiveness is a valid construct: SLES explains about half the variation in NC expert rankings, and lagged SLES persists (rho 0.38 when majority entered, 0.40 when minority entered, 0.66 with no change in control). Effectiveness reflects innate or cultivated lawmaking ability as well as position.
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/compute_pillars.py lines 181-183 form the score from weighted leg, press, influence and demo terms; fec/engine/pillar_policy.py lines 11-16 hold Leg 0.45, Press 0.10, Influence 0.40, Demo 0.05. fec/members/lep_criterion.py lines 17-19 define bar B: rho at least 0.30 convergent, 0.15 to 0.30 weak, below 0.15 null. The +0.10 orthogonality value and n are recorded only in the brain, which was not read in this check.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The persistence and NC validity figures are from the state paper and do not validate the federal blend. The orthogonality reading depends on CEL LES being the federal analogue. Under bar B, +0.10 falls in the null band, which matches the rel's wording, but the +0.10 value itself was not verified.
bearings.verifier_note: Quote and persistence numbers reproduce. The +0.10 value, its n and the brain attribution were not verified because the brain was not read. Code bar B is +0.30 convergent and below +0.15 null, consistent with the rel. Softened only because the key number rests on an unchecked brain note.

bearings.paper_claim: Bill advancement is tilted toward majority members (+0.370 pooled, 58 percent above minority mean), chairs (+0.507 pooled; 0.609 lower, 0.307 upper), senior members (+0.032 per term) and moderates (distance from median -0.114). These are associational estimates; the paper does not measure effort and does not show that low minority advancement reflects position rather than effort.
bearings.paper_location: Table 1 lines 896-1027 (pp. 26-27); associational caveat p. 34 lines 1735-1737
bearings.system_side: fec/moneyball_core.py lines 901-925 (overall_say_do_gate): Champion is capped to Ally when the member has at least 10 direct sponsored bills and an advancement rate at or below 0.20, unless the exceptional authorship case applies (at least 20 direct bills with full top-tier delivery), or when breadth or coverage fails. It fails open when the bill source is unavailable. It changes the displayed tier, not rank. No adjustment for majority, chair or seniority.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The coefficients are state-level pooled estimates and must carry strata or labels. A low advancement rate is not evidence of cheap talk without a within-chamber, majority-adjusted baseline, so the rel's caution holds.
bearings.verifier_note: Coefficients reproduce (Table 1 lines 906-961; session and seniority lines 1883-1961). The rel gets the gate direction wrong: it is a cap triggered when the advancement rate is at or below 0.20, not a requirement of at least 20 percent. The position-not-effort reading is overreach.

related.why: Both are measures of which legislators get bills advanced. This paper does not cite Sotoudeh, so the link is the analyst's inference, not a citation.
Both study US state legislators using state bill-sponsorship records. The paper does not cite Fouirnaies and Hall, so the same-data label is downgraded to complements.

summary_issues: Summary calls both chamber-level studies exploratory. The paper frames only Study 2 as exploratory (lines 1726-1732); Study 1 tests two named hypotheses, conditional party government and insecure majorities (lines 1234-1236, 1434-1435).

Summary says the shadow departs from SLES in two ways. The bearing lists more: cosponsor credit with 180-day timing decay, letters forced to weight 5, a 70/30 composite, and significance from upstream impact data. The claim that significance comes from CU mention frequency was not found in legislative_effectiveness.py.
Gaps section says majority status is the largest structural driver of advancement. Not supported: the pooled chair estimate 0.507 exceeds the majority estimate 0.370 (Table 1 lines 914 and 921).

Ext key finding on Study 1 says a smaller seat-share imbalance widens the majority advantage, which it calls the reverse of the insecure-majority expectation. The paper reads the negative imbalance coefficient (-0.529) as support for insecure majorities (lines 1417-1420, 1459-1461).

Ext key finding says longer sessions are linked to a smaller seniority gap among majority members. Table 3 column 3.3 gives -0.046, not significant; the significant -0.071 is the minority column 3.4 (lines 1893-1896). The same ext also says session length is not significant in the freshman-seniority gap, so ext contradicts itself.

Summary calls the live efficiency term a hit-rate measure that the paper outperforms. The paper's hit-rate comparison is SLES against hit rates in North Carolina; mapping that to the Melange efficiency term is the analyst's inference.

Paul alignment and brain claims are not checked here: paul_entries is empty, the brain was not read under the boot-skip rule, and the claims about Paul's citations, the September shadow commission, the +0.10 CEL LES orthogonality and the not-activated shadow status are unverified and remain open.
Related links: the text does not mention Aref and Neal, Ramey, or Porter, so those three links were dropped. Sotoudeh and Fouirnaies were kept as complements only, not as citations.

Bearing 5 and the gaps section state or imply that minority advancement reflects position rather than effort; the paper measures no effort and is associational (p. 34). The causal reading was removed.

Coverage: the text file was read at the cited lines for all five bearings and all five related links. The Supplementary Appendix and PDF were not available, so Table A4 (NC validation), Table A9 (term limits) and Table A10 were not checked; Figure 6 at p. 30 was not checked.
